questions.cardText:
[Geology] Which of the following is NOT a fossil?
A. A petrified piece of wood
B. A footprint in rock
C. A remnant of a comet
Answer: C. Fossils are the preserved remains or traces of ancient organisms, such as bones, shells, and even footprints. In contrast, a remnant of a comet is a piece of a celestial body from space, unrelated to the biological processes that create fossils.
questions.de: Wie nennt man ein Fossil, das statt des Körpers die Aktivität eines urzeitlichen Lebewesens festhält, etwa einen Fußabdruck oder eine Grabspur im Gestein?
questions.en: What is a fossil called that records an ancient organism's activity, such as a footprint or burrow in rock, rather than its body?

timeline.labelEn: Charles Darwin publishes his book on earthworms and soil, a very early work on ichnology
timeline.labelDe: Charles Darwin veröffentlicht sein Buch über Regenwürmer und Bodenbildung, ein sehr frühes Werk der Ichnologie

questions.notes: 'Which is NOT a fossil' reworked to the underlying fact behind the footprint option: fossils include traces as well as remains. Wikipedia contrasts trace fossils with body fossils.

questions.cardText:
[Physiology and Anatomy] What is the fattiest organ in a healthy human being?
A. Skin  B. Brain  C. Liver
Answer: B. The brain is the fattiest organ in a typical and healthy human body, consisting of about 60% fat. This fat is crucial for brain health, playing a key role in insulating neurons and ensuring efficient signal transmission.
questions.de: Welches Organ ist das fetthaltigste im gesunden menschlichen Körper und besteht angeblich zu etwa 60 % aus Fett?
questions.en: Which organ is the fattiest in a healthy human body, often said to be about 60% fat?

timeline.labelEn: Rudolf Virchow coins the word myelin for the fatty insulation of nerve fibres
timeline.labelDe: Rudolf Virchow prägt das Wort Myelin für die fetthaltige Isolierung der Nervenfasern

questions.notes: Guinness World Records lists the brain as the fattiest organ, 'typically composed of 60% fat', but the same page says by weight water is c. 77% and lipids 10–12%; the 60% figure refers to dry weight. Timeline (Virchow, myelin) from Wikipedia 'Myelin'.
